title: Metabolic Pathways — Carbohydrate, Lipid, Protein, Vitamin and Mineral Metabolism
shortDescription: The energy-yielding and biosynthetic pathways in one connected map.
genZNote: Metabolism is the group project where everyone hands off to acetyl-CoA. Know which step happens where and how much ATP it pays.

table.caption: Key pathways
rows: Per acetyl-CoA: 3 NADH, 1 FADH2, 1 GTP/ATP, 2 CO2
Makes glucose from lactate, glycerol, amino acids

sections.heading: Lipid Metabolism
bullets: β-oxidation of fatty acids in mitochondria yields acetyl-CoA, NADH and FADH2 (palmitate ≈ 106 ATP net).
Lipogenesis in the fed state; lipolysis by hormone-sensitive lipase in the fasting state.
Ketone bodies (acetoacetate, β-hydroxybutyrate) from excess acetyl-CoA in starvation/uncontrolled diabetes.
Cholesterol synthesis (HMG-CoA reductase — statin target); lipoproteins: chylomicrons, VLDL, LDL, HDL.

sections.heading: Protein, Vitamin and Mineral Metabolism
bullets: Transamination (PLP/B6) moves amino groups; oxidative deamination releases ammonia; the urea cycle in liver converts ammonia to urea.
Glucogenic vs ketogenic amino acids; nitrogen balance (positive in growth/pregnancy).
Vitamins as coenzymes: B1 (TPP) in PDH, B2 (FAD), B3 (NAD), B5 (CoA), B7 (biotin carboxylation), B6 (transamination), B9/B12 (one-carbon and methylmalonyl).
Minerals: Mg/Mn as cofactors, Fe in cytochromes, Zn in dehydrogenases, I in thyroid hormone regulating basal metabolism.
Fed vs fasted state: insulin promotes storage, glucagon/adrenaline mobilise.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Metabolism is the integrated set of catabolic and anabolic pathways that convert nutrients into energy (ATP), storage forms and structural components.
keyFacts: TCA per acetyl-CoA: 3 NADH, 1 FADH2, 1 GTP.

highYieldFacts: Insulin lowers blood glucose; glucagon raises it.
commonTraps: Do not say TCA occurs in cytosol.

questions.explanation: Fat oxidation produces acetyl-CoA beyond TCA capacity.
